title: Fall Prevention at Home for Seniors: A Room-by-Room Checklist
short_title: Fall prevention at home, room by room
description: More than 1 in 4 older adults fall each year, but most falls can be prevented. Here's a room-by-room walkthrough to make Mom or Dad's home safer: the bathroom, stairs and entryways, the kitchen and living room, and the bedroom. Plus what to do after a fall, and when it's time for help at home.

parts.head: Fall prevention at home, room by room
parts.sub: Make Mom or Dad's home safer this week
parts.text: More than one in four older adults fall each year. But most falls can be prevented. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's how to make Mom or Dad's home safer, room by room.

parts.head: It's rarely just one thing
parts.sub: Weak muscles, vision, medicines, lighting, clutter
parts.text: Falls are rarely caused by one thing. Weak muscles, vision changes, medicine side effects like dizziness, poor lighting, and things in the way, like loose rugs or clutter, all add up.

parts.head: The bathroom
parts.sub: Grab bars, a non-slip mat, a shower chair
parts.text: Start with the bathroom, the riskiest room in the house. Add grab bars by the toilet and in the shower, a non-slip mat, and a shower chair if standing for long is hard. A raised toilet seat can help, too.

parts.head: Stairs and entryways
parts.sub: Handrails on both sides, bright lights, even walkways
parts.text: Next, stairs and entryways. Sturdy handrails on both sides, bright lights at the top and bottom, and non-slip treads. Outside, fix cracked steps, and keep walkways lit.

parts.head: Kitchen and living room
parts.sub: Things within reach. No loose rugs or cords.
parts.text: In the kitchen and living room, move everyday things to between waist and shoulder height, so no step stool is needed. Take up loose rugs, keep cords out of walkways, and choose a sturdy chair with arms over a soft couch.

parts.head: The bedroom
parts.sub: A lit path, a nightlight, a phone by the bed
parts.text: In the bedroom, make a clear, lit path to the bathroom, with a nightlight. And keep a phone or call button within reach of the bed. The middle of the night is the riskiest time.

parts.head: Plan about an hour
parts.text: Plan about an hour to walk through the whole house. Most of these fixes are easy.

parts.head: See a doctor, even without an injury
parts.sub: Ask about a fall-risk medication review
parts.text: If a fall has already happened, see a doctor, even if there's no obvious injury. A fall is often a sign of something else, like a medicine problem, an infection, or a vision change. Ask about a fall-risk medication review.

parts.head: A second fall raises the risk
parts.sub: Time for an honest conversation about help
parts.text: A second fall raises the risk of a serious injury. If it's happened more than once, it's time for an honest conversation about some help.

parts.head: Signs it's time for help
parts.sub: Repeated falls, an injury, or living alone
parts.text: Repeated falls, a fall with an injury, or a fall while living alone are all signs that help at home could make a real difference, from a few hours a week to overnight care.

parts.head: Steady hands, and a safe plan
parts.sub: Our caregivers never lift someone after a fall
parts.text: Our caregivers help with walking, safe transfers, and bathing, and keep an eye out for hazards. And if someone does fall, our caregivers never try to lift them. They stay with them, check for injury, keep them comfortable, call nine one one if they're hurt, and call our office every time.
Call us at (417) 234-8494, or visit mo-care.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
